rule: R6 Stack: R1 (first CNO-family c/w look inside 2..360 min to the start with listed EV >= 2.5%) AND first c/w look of the bet <= 360 min to the start AND entry-look cost < 0.50 (plus money)
numbers_reproduced: REPRODUCES EXACTLY. Own re-implementation from the expr with the shared loader: R1 184 bets / 44 games; R6 119 bets / 40 games, 74 with a close in 32 games (45 bets = 38% have no close), 71 close_ok in 31 games. CLV at the entry look's price: all closes 3.211% [2.296%, 4.530%] (builder 3.211% [2.328%, 4.451%]; CI differs only by bootstrap draw), beat-the-close share 0.811; close_ok 3.209% [2.316%, 4.513%]. ROI at the look price -2.887% (115 settled, 38 games) [-26.4%, +22.4%] (builder -2.887%): uninformative. 52.7 bets/day, 17.7 games/day over the 2.256-day span. Rest of R1 (65 bets, 42 closes, 21 games) 1.37%; R6 minus rest +1.84 pts [+0.79, +3.19] game-cluster bootstrap (builder +1.84 [+0.78, +3.24]); close_ok version +1.58 pts [+0.51, +3.02]. Independent closes (close_ok, non-Tracker: 15 Novig-trades >=3 trades + 3 ESPN + 1 Pinnacle) 19 closes / 14 games +1.30% [+0.52%, +2.40%], one-sided bootstrap p(<=0)=0.0014 (builder 0.0013). Tracker closes 52 / 23 games +3.91% [+2.85%, +5.44%] (builder 3.91%). Builder's halves 2.43% / 3.43% reproduce only with a calendar cut Oct 3 | Oct 4-5 (16 closes/13 games vs 58 closes/19 games), NOT with the loader's equal-games split_by_date (cut Oct 4): first half 84 bets / 34 games, 62 closes / 28 games, 3.11% [2.13, 4.68]; second half 35 bets / 6 games, 12 closes / 4 games, 3.75% [3.35, 4.64]. Per first-look day: Oct 3 2.43% (16 closes/13 games), Oct 4 3.34% (46/15), Oct 5 3.75% (12/4). Builder's 'baseline CLV 0.02604' NOT reproduced by any natural definition (R1 at look = 2.545% all closes / 2.669% close_ok; R1 at first-listed price 1.639%; all bets with a close at first price 0.19% [-0.36, 0.79] on 683 closes / 69 games). No NaN silently dropped: 0 NaN in ev, american, minToStart over 38,997 c/w look rows; NaN closeFair only removes bets from CLV (45 of 119). No look-ahead found: the selection uses only that look's ev, cost, minToStart and the first look's minToStart.
reason: The numbers reproduce, but the claim that the stack is a credible improvement over R1 rests on evidence that cannot carry it. (1) 70% of R6's closes (52 of 74) are Tracker closes = CNO's own book consensus re-read before the start, which exist almost only for bets Tj placed (52 of 53 placed). For them CLV ~ the listed EV (mean EV 3.74%, mean CLV 3.91%, mean CLV-EV +0.17 pts, corr 0.03): it says the soft-book consensus did not drift, not that the bet beat a sharp market. Across all 228 Tracker closes the CLV is only 0.57%. (2) On the independent closes (19, 14 games; only 1 Pinnacle close in the whole rule, so a sharp close is untested) R6 is +1.30% but the stack's advantage over the rest of R1 is +1.15 pts [-1.44, +3.08], p(<=0)=0.16, and over all of R1 only +0.49 pts [-0.60, +1.42]; R1 itself is +0.81% [-0.04, +2.13] on 33 closes / 23 games. (3) All 19 independent closes are in the first half; the second half (Oct 5: 35 bets, 6 games, 12 closes in 4 games) has zero independent closes and its 3.75% is Tracker-only, against 3.11% for the rest of R1 (6 closes, 3 games) and 3.54% for all of R1 (18 closes, 5 games): it cannot tell the stack from R1. (4) The three conditions were picked together on the same 2.26 days (builder tried 522 variants); the 2x2 is super-additive in a way that looks fitted: fresh&plus 3.21% (74 closes), fresh&not-plus 0.74% (18), stale&plus 1.47% (21), stale&not-plus 4.48% (3). What does hold: the effect is not an artifact of a few games, scanner gaps, or NaN handling (see caveats). A rule that only removes bets from R1 breaks no safety limit, so it is a QUESTION FOR TJ only after more data; today the data suggests R1 (EV>=2.5%) is mildly positive vs independent closes and the stack's extra ~0.7 pts per bet is unproven.
caveats: Second half is tiny: Oct 5 only, 35 bets in 6 games, 12 closes in 4 games (18 of the 35 bets are in ONE game), all Tracker closes, so its narrow CI [3.35, 4.64] reflects 4 games, not precision. Per-day CLV (Oct 3 / 4 / 5) = 2.43 / 3.34 / 3.75, all positive but fitted in-sample.

Builder's half split (first 16 closes, second 58) is a different cut from the loader's equal-games split (62 vs 12 closes); both should be reported, neither is out of sample for a rule chosen on all 2.26 days.

Independent close evidence: 19 closes = 15 Novig-last-trades (>=3 trades; a Novig price converging, subset CLV 0.75% [-0.21, 1.87]) + 3 ESPN/DraftKings (3.33%) + 1 Pinnacle. Novig publishes trades the next morning, so no independent close exists for Oct 5 games yet.

Tracker closes are CNO's consensus (not a sharp line), exist for 52 of the 53 bets Tj placed, and so are a placed-bet subset: ROI of bets with a close -13.8% (72 settled, 32 games) vs no close +15.4% (43 settled, 20 games): noise (CIs -37..+19, -20..+52) but the monetised result for the Tracker-closed bets is negative.

Concentration: one NFL game holds 23 of 119 bets and 20 of 74 closes (27%); the top 2 games hold 41 bets; NFL 69 bets (58%), NHL 32; player props 101 of 119. Leave-one-game-out CLV range 3.01% to 3.83% (all 70+ closes); dropping the top-2 games by closes 3.86% [2.84, 4.81] (48 closes/30 games); dropping the top-5 3.51% [2.40, 4.62]; 28 of 32 games with closes are positive, game-equal-weight mean 3.67%. So not driven by one game, but one slate (Sunday NFL props + NHL).

Freshness is not a scanner-gap artifact: 45 of 119 R6 bets were first seen within 15 min of a >30 min gap in scanning (the app was off ~04:21-10:20 and ~02:28-10:02); excluding them CLV is 2.64% [1.75, 4.58] on 44 closes / 18 games (excluding first 3 / 10 / 30 / 60 min: 2.70 / 2.68 / 2.62 / 2.49%). The first sighting at study start (Oct 3 17:56) is left-censored for ~7 bets.

Entry look: 52 of 119 entries are a later look than the first (EV at first look < 2.5% for 51), their CLV is 2.76% [1.94, 3.54] (35 closes) vs 3.61% [1.89, 5.76] for entry at the first look (39 closes); CLV at the first-listed price is 2.56% vs 3.21% at the entry look. Tj's own fills were within +0.19 pts of the look cost (81% at or better), CLV at his placed price 3.53%.

Game-level random-split experiment (NOT a date split, same 2.26 days): choosing the best (first-look cap, cost cap) cell of a 36-cell grid on a random half of games gave +2.18 pts in the training half and +1.36 pts over the rest in the held-out half (90.7% of 1000 splits positive; +0.55 pts vs R1 as a whole); the fixed R6 rule beat the rest of R1 in 99.9% of random half-of-games subsets (mean +1.92 pts). Shows the stack is not a few-games fluke, not that it holds on future days.

Single conditions inside R1 (CLV at look): fresh 2.73% (92 closes/38 games) vs not fresh 1.84% (24/13); plus money 2.83% (95/35) vs not plus 1.27% (21/14). R6 vs fresh-but-not-plus +2.47 pts [+1.23, +4.10] (18 closes), vs plus-but-stale +1.74 [+0.19, +3.64] (21 closes): the incremental value of the combination vs either alone rests on 18-21 closes in 12-14 games each.
Stake capacity: median Novig $ available at the price $50 (mean $243, total $28.96k over 119 bets); entry-look dollars median $47. Per day ~53 bets in ~18 games.

What would settle it: a fresh sample with independent closes (Pinnacle/ESPN/Novig trades >=3) of about 85 games per arm to detect a 1.15-pt advantage of the stack over the rest of R1 at 80% power (one-sided 0.05; game-mean SD ~2.2 to 3.6 pts), about 110 games per arm for 1.0 pt; at the first-half rate (14 independent games per 2 days) that is several weeks. Cheaper: keep logging and compare R6 vs R1 on Oct 6+ games only, pre-registered, with the Pinnacle-close share reported.
Builder's baseline CLV 0.02604 could not be matched to any population I tried (about 100 variants of window/EV threshold); it should be restated.
